types.summary: National parks are for enjoying and studying nature: no pets, camping is usually in campgrounds, and hunting and plant picking are banned.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed. Assistance animals are. You can drive through on a public road with a pet if you don't stop and it stays in the car.

camping.note: Usually in campgrounds. Bush camping is allowed in some parks; check signs.

fishing.note: Where a park allows it, you need a NSW recreational fishing licence. Check the park's page for gear limits.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Only where the park's plan of management or written NPWS consent allows it. Hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Handheld detectors, only as part of fossicking where it is allowed.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

fires.note: Only in designated fireplaces, and not allowed in every park. Check before you go.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Nature reserves exist mainly to protect ecosystems: no pets, no fossicking and no hunting.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed. Assistance animals are. You can drive through on a public road with a pet if you don't stop and it stays in the car.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Fossicking consent is never considered for nature reserves.

metal detecting.note: Metal detecting counts as fossicking, which is never considered for nature reserves.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: State conservation areas are open for visits and may allow mining; pets are banned, but a few (like Torrington) allow fossicking.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed. Assistance animals are. You can drive through on a public road with a pet if you don't stop and it stays in the car.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Only where the area's plan of management allows it. Hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Handheld detectors only as part of fossicking, where fossicking is allowed.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Regional parks are for recreation, and some allow on-leash dog walking.

dogs.note: On a leash, only in designated dog-walking areas; the park's plan of management decides where. Check the park's page.

fishing.note: Where a park allows it, you need a NSW recreational fishing licence.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Only where the park's plan of management or written NPWS consent allows it. Hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Handheld detectors, only as part of fossicking where it is allowed.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Aboriginal areas protect places of cultural importance to Aboriginal people: no pets and no fossicking.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed. Assistance animals are. You can drive through on a public road with a pet if you don't stop and it stays in the car.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Fossicking consent is never considered for Aboriginal areas.

metal detecting.note: Metal detecting counts as fossicking, which is never considered for Aboriginal areas.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Historic sites protect heritage places; some 'living' villages such as Hill End and Hartley allow dogs on a leash.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed, except on a leash in the living villages of Hill End and Hartley.

camping.note: Some historic sites have campgrounds, e.g. Hill End.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Fossicking consent is never considered for historic sites.

metal detecting.note: Metal detecting counts as fossicking, which is never considered for historic sites.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Karst conservation reserves protect important cave areas: no pets, and fossicking only at Grove Creek.

dogs.note: Pets aren't allowed. Assistance animals are. You can drive through on a public road with a pet if you don't stop and it stays in the car.

foraging.note: The NPWS page bans picking plants and flowers but doesn't mention mushrooms or fruit. Ask the park office.

fossicking.note: Not in karst reserves, except one part of Abercrombie.

metal detecting.note: Only as part of fossicking, which karst reserves don't allow except one part of Abercrombie.

hunting.note: Hunting isn't allowed on NPWS land, except for Aboriginal people under native title arrangements.

plants.note: Picking flowers or collecting plants is illegal in parks.

types.summary: Flora reserves are State forest land permanently reserved to conserve native plants.
State forests welcome dogs and allow free camping almost everywhere; fossicking and hunting need permission.

dogs.note: Welcome in all State forests. Keep your dog under control and pick up after it.

camping.note: Free in all State forests except Cumberland and Strickland. Not in picnic areas. Usually up to four weeks.

fishing.note: You need a recreational fishing permit.

foraging.note: Mushrooms: picking for your own use needs no permit; selling needs one. Bush rock can't be removed.

fossicking.note: Needs a Forestry Corporation authorisation ($27.50, 12 months, statewide). Not in quarries; check the map for areas where it's not allowed.

metal detecting.note: Covered by the State forest fossicking permit, which includes gold hunting with metal detectors.

hunting.note: Only in forests declared and open for hunting, with a valid hunting licence and written permission.

fires.note: Many forests ban wood and charcoal fires during high fire danger; check the forest's fire ban table. Where allowed, keep fires under 1 m² and 4.5 m from logs and trees.

types.summary: National parks are for conserving nature: no pets, camping needs a permit, and fossicking and metal detecting are banned.

dogs.note: No dogs, cats or other pets. You can drive through on gazetted roads with your dog inside the car, without stopping. Certified support dogs are allowed.

camping.note: You need a camping permit before you camp, and must display your tag.

fishing.note: Allowed only in some national parks and sometimes only in parts of them. Queensland fishing rules apply; some dams need a Stocked Impoundment Permit.

fossicking.note: Fossicking isn't allowed in national parks.

metal detecting.note: Using a metal detector is prohibited in protected areas.

hunting.note: You can't use firearms in any Queensland park or forest.

fires.note: Only in existing QPWS fireplaces, fire rings or fire spots, and never during fire bans. Don't collect firewood.

plants.note: You must not collect plants, rocks, shells or soil (including picking flowers or gathering firewood) without an authority.

types.summary: Conservation parks protect nature; some allow dogs on a leash, camping needs a permit, and fossicking is banned.

dogs.note: Only in some conservation parks, on a leash. Check the park's page and signs.

camping.note: You need a camping permit before you camp, and must display your tag.

fishing.note: Allowed under Queensland fishing rules unless a park notice says otherwise. No threatened fish or spiny crays, and no mud crabs for bait.

fossicking.note: Fossicking isn't allowed in conservation parks.

metal detecting.note: Using a metal detector is prohibited in protected areas.

hunting.note: You can't use firearms in any Queensland park or forest.

fires.note: Only in existing QPWS fireplaces, fire rings or fire spots, and never during fire bans. Don't collect firewood.

plants.note: You must not collect plants, rocks, shells or soil (including picking flowers or gathering firewood) without an authority.

types.summary: Resources reserves are protected areas that allow some controlled use; licensed fossicking and fossicking camping are outside the park rules there.

dogs.note: Only where a notice at the entrance says dog-walking is allowed. Keep your dog under control.

camping.note: You need a camping permit (or camping under the Fossicking Act).

fishing.note: Allowed under Queensland fishing rules unless a notice says otherwise. No threatened fish or spiny crays, and no mud crabs for bait.

fossicking.note: You need a Queensland fossicking licence; the protected area rules don't apply to licensed fossicking in a resources reserve.

metal detecting.note: Only while fossicking under a fossicking licence; otherwise metal detectors need written approval in protected areas.

hunting.note: You can't use firearms in any Queensland park or forest.

fires.note: Not in a fire ban area or where a notice bans fires. Use a provided fireplace or a spot more than 2 m from anything flammable, and put it out before you leave.

plants.note: You must not collect plants, rocks, shells or soil (including picking flowers or gathering firewood) without an authority.

types.summary: State forests allow dogs on a leash in some places; camping needs a permit, and fossicking is only allowed in general permission areas.

dogs.note: Only in some State forests, on a leash. Dogs can stay overnight at only a few camping areas.

camping.note: You need a camping permit before you camp, and must display your tag.

fishing.note: Allowed in some parks and forests; Queensland fishing rules apply.

fossicking.note: Only in general permission areas, and you need a fossicking licence.

metal detecting.note: Metal detectors count as fossicking hand tools, so only in general permission areas with a fossicking licence.

hunting.note: You can't use firearms in any Queensland park or forest, and you need a permit to bring one into a State forest.

fires.note: Only in existing QPWS fireplaces, fire rings or fire spots, and never during fire bans. Don't collect firewood.

plants.note: All plants, animals and natural resources are protected and must not be disturbed or damaged.

types.summary: Signposted areas set up for fossicking, where you need a fossicking licence but not the landowner's permission.

dogs.note: Don't bring animals where a notice bans them.

camping.note: Only in some areas (e.g. Rubyvale, Sapphire, Opalton, Duck Creek) with a fossicking camping permit. Stay up to 3 months.

fossicking.note: You need a fossicking licence. Hand tools only; no machinery. Don't dig deeper than 2 m.

metal detecting.note: Metal detectors count as hand tools for fossicking, so you need a fossicking licence.

hunting.note: Don't use a weapon, trap or explosive on designated fossicking land or areas.

fires.note: Only in a fireplace or a cleared space at least 2 m around, and not where a notice or ban stops fires.

fossicking.note: Allowed in all of Torrington, with hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Handheld detectors are allowed as part of fossicking.

fossicking.note: Allowed, except beside Tuena Creek. Hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Handheld detectors as part of fossicking, except beside Tuena Creek.

fossicking.note: Only in the Grove Creek part of the reserve. Hand tools only.

metal detecting.note: Only as part of fossicking in the Grove Creek part.
